newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court maintains potato starch production quota system.
newsitem.headline: Court maintains potato starch production quota system.

text.p: The European Court of First Instance dismissed on Thursday an attempt by French potato starch manufacturer Roquette Freres SA to annul the Council of Ministers' potato starch production quota system.
Under the quota system, each member state is allocated a quota calculated on the basis of the average quantity of potato starch produced in marketing years 1990 through 1993.
Roquette alleged the quota system was discriminatory, as it gave Germany special treatment and infringed principles of proportionality.
The Council and the Commission denied the admissibility of Roquette's claim and the court reviewed the right of individuals to challenge Community institution decisions.

Noting the right of individuals to challenge a decision which individually and directly concerns them, the court distinguished the right to challenge a regulation from the right to challenge decisions.

"The test for distinguishing between a regulation and a decision is whether or not the measure in question has general application, and it is applied by assessing the nature of the contested decision and in particular the legal effects which it is intended to produce or actually produces," the court said.

The court found the potato starch quota system regulation to have been determined objectively, to apply in a general and abstract manner and to be unaffected by a system which gives Germany special treatment.

The court rejected Roquette's argument that it was individually concerned because it applies to a limited number of ascertained traders. "The mere fact that a trader forms part of a closed group of traders ... is not in itself sufficient for the trader in question to have to be regarded as individually concerned," the court said.
(Court translation into English. Original language of the case: French)
"Common agricultural policy - Quota system in relation to the production of potato starch - Regulation (EC) No 1868/94 - Action for annulment - Closed group of traders - Inadmissibility"
Case T-298/94
Roquette Freres SA, applicant
v
Council of the European Union, defendant
supported by
Commission of the European Communities, intervener
application for annulment of Council regulation (EC) No 1868/94 of 27 July 1994 establishing a quota system in relation to the production of potato starch (OJ 1994 L 197, p. 4)
THE COURT OF FIRST INSTANCE hereby
1. Dismisses the application as inadmissible;
2. Orders the applicant to pay its own costs and those of the Council;
3. Orders the Commission to bear its own costs.
